summary: A speculative analysis of DTCC/NSCC settlement mechanics and proposed GME price cycles. The author describes SLD cycles tied to options expiration, C+21/C+35 calendar-day cycles, and theoretical FTD-hiding mechanisms. The core thesis posits that these cycles drive predictable price movements and speculates that RC might trigger mandatory corporate reorganizations to force short buyins. Multiple claims are explicitly labeled with low confidence (3-9/10). By 2026, the cycle predictions proved unreliable, RC never triggered the hypothesized corporate events, and GameStop's NFT marketplace was shut down rather than used for share counting.

key_claims.claim: SLD cycles tied to monthly options expiration create predictable price movements in GME
key_claims.note: Author rates own SLD cycle confidence 9/10 (p. 3-15). SLD cycles exist as real DTCC mechanisms; however, author admits most are 'nothingburgers' and cycle-predicted price movement never validated through 2026. No rigorous statistical evidence provided.

key_claims.claim: C+21 calendar-day cycles used to move GME but no longer do due to stock growth
key_claims.note: Author rates C+21 confidence 3/10 (p. 10), calls it 'mostly horse shit.' Subjective observation without falsifiable mechanism. No predictive validation shown through 2026.

key_claims.claim: C+35 calendar-day cycles continue to move GME in rare cases
key_claims.note: Author rates C+35 confidence 4.5/10 (p. 10). Charts provided without statistical rigor. Claimed effects never demonstrated as reliable through 2026.

key_claims.claim: FTDs can be hidden via One-Day Settling (ODS) exemption and moved between members
key_claims.note: ODS exemption exists (p. 14-15); however, the mechanism for repeatedly shifting shorts between complicit members to avoid CNS processing is theoretical and unverified. Author provides no evidence this occurs in practice.

key_claims.claim: Obligations can be permanently marked X-REORG to exempt shorts from forced buyins triggered by corporate reorganization
key_claims.note: Pages 16-17 present this as potential mechanism. Author includes 'Big Fucking Warning' (p. 13) stating 'not 100% verified.' No evidence this exemption is actually used or effective.

key_claims.claim: RC will trigger a mandatory corporate event (merger/reorganization) to force all short obligations to close, resulting in MOASS
key_claims.note: Pages 17-18 speculate about '4D Chess RC.' By 2026, GameStop never executed any such reorganization, merger, or forced-close trigger. Prediction deadline passed without fulfillment.

key_claims.claim: NFT marketplace and proper share counting will force shorts to close their positions
key_claims.note: Page 18. GameStop launched an NFT marketplace in 2022 but shut it down in 2024. No share-counting mechanism emerged. Prediction clearly failed by 2026.

key_claims.claim: DTCC/NSCC does not mark or tag shares; they are pooled for liquidity with no inventory
key_claims.note: Page 18. Accurate description of DTCC operational structure—shares are not individually tracked, enabling lending and liquidity pools.

validity_rationale: The work correctly describes some real DTCC/NSCC mechanisms but builds an unproven thesis that settlement cycles predictably drive GME price. Core predictions—RC triggering reorganization, NFT-based forced closes, C+21/C+35 cycle reliability—all failed by 2026. The author explicitly rates own confidence low (3-9/10) and acknowledges claims are unverified. No causal mechanism demonstrated; primarily chart pattern-matching. By 2026, the cycle theory produced no predictive power and RC never executed the hypothesized moves."
